text:
lin: saw another pattern where streaming clients block waiting for tokens, upstream stalls mid-response and retries just pile up. thinking of an adaptive truncate+hedge design where clients can advertise a tolerance window and edge will either truncate+tag or hedge to a warmer model.
rachel: client-specified tolerance? curious how that interacts with 3rd-party SDKs. example header?
lin: header X-Stream-Tolerance-ms, default 500ms. If no tokens emitted in tolerance window, edge emits a 'truncated' event/frame and either: (A) return buffered tokens + synthetic suffix, or (B) launch a local hedged request to a smaller model and stream that result.
omar: Tradeoffs: (A) faster but risk of confusing downstream aggregators; (B) more compute & complexity, may increase cost. Need route opt-in.
sean: Also need side-effect guardrails: only allow for pure inference/read endpoints. For calls that may trigger webhooks we must NOT truncate.
jena: Observability: add metrics edge.truncate.count, edge.hedge.launch.count, edge.truncate.reason, trace tag edge.truncate=true. Include the tolerance value in span attrs.
lin: pseudo-proto: ```
# on edge request start
tolerance = request.headers.get('X-Stream-Tolerance-ms', 500)
start_timer()
while streaming:
  if not upstream_emitted and timer.elapsed >= tolerance:
    if route.allows_hedge and tenant_policy.allows_hedge:
      launch_hedge(small_model)
      tag span edge.truncate=hedge
    else:
      emit_truncated_frame(suffix='[truncated: upstream slow]')
      tag span edge.truncate=partial
    break
```
rachel: A few notes: 1) billing accounting: if we hedge, bill both attempts but label primary_failed=true. 2) telemetry must capture latency delta and token counts per-path.
omar: We should avoid hedging to models that might diverge semantically; pick deterministically cheaper variants with same model family. Also add confidence sampling to compare quality.
deploy-bot: notice: alert: upstream.replica_failures > 5% for 2min in eu-central -> linked incident #5432
sean: Rollout: start with truncate-only mode (no hedging) on internal dev routes. If metrics show truncation reduces 499s and improves p50 latency, can A/B hedging later.
lina: (typo) lin: +1 start truncate-only. Also add per-tenant budget for hedging in config to prevent runaway cost.
rachel: SDK: add Stream.on('truncated', info) callback and expose headers X-Edge-Truncated and X-Edge-Hedge. Backcompat: ignore by default.
lin: edge config knobs: route.enable_truncate(bool), route.tolerance_ms(default 500), route.hedge_enabled(bool), route.hedge_models(list), tenant.hedge_budget_tokens.
jenA: (typo) jena: We need an invariants doc: truncation must never suppress server-verified side-effects and must preserve idempotency markers.
sean: Also consider a safety cooldown: if tenant experiences > 3 truncates/sec for 1m, auto-disable hedging and escalate.
omar: instrumentation: create a lightweight evaluation harness to score hedged vs primary outputs for a sample of requests to detect quality regressions. log sample diffs with bucketed reasons.
rachel: security: ensure truncated/synthetic payloads are clearly tagged so downstream logging systems don't mistakenly index them as full model output. mask in audit logs? maybe tag with meta field.
lin: I'll draft an RFC with state machine (Idle -> AwaitingFirstToken -> Truncated -> Hedging) and metrics. will include histograms for tolerance vs observed stall.
jenA: assign owners: lin -> RFC + edge prototype, rachel -> SDK + billing mapping, omar -> hedging model list & eval harness, sean -> rollout/runbook.
lin: thanks. starting a small PR to add header parsing and truncate frame. will start the truncate-only canary at 0.5% on dev routes.
deploy-bot: reminder: follow-up review scheduled in 10 days. :calendar:
